questions.answer: Not settled. The documents say the exception is raised when no PCPI core acknowledges within 16 clock cycles, and that pcpi_wait, kept asserted until pcpi_ready, prevents the illegal instruction exception. They do not say which event starts the 16-cycle count (pcpi_valid assertion is not stated), whether pcpi_wait suspends the timeout indefinitely, or what happens if pcpi_wait is first asserted after cycle 16.

Not settled. 'More than a couple of cycles' is not quantified, and 'as soon as the instruction has been decoded successfully' has no cycle bound. The only hard limit given is the 16-cycle acknowledgement window. The designer must define the thresholds.

Not settled. The documents say pcpi_ready is asserted when execution finishes and that optionally a result is written to pcpi_rd with pcpi_wr asserted. They do not give the timing of pcpi_wr relative to pcpi_ready, and do not say whether pcpi_rd is sampled only when pcpi_ready is high. The designer must specify this.

Not settled. The RISC-V text gives the rdh/rdq register restrictions as part of the recommended code sequence, so that microarchitectures can fuse the pair. It does not say what hardware must do when they are violated, and it does not say whether a testbench should check that case. The designer must decide whether these are software-only constraints.
